questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that the destination of my exchange was in Europe so I was able to get the Eramus money. I also wanted to go to a relatively safe country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university provided me with a lot of information. It was really helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We had introduction days where I met a lot of other international students. I also had a coordinator who I could always reach if i needed help with anything at the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty hard. A lot of people struggled with finding accommodations. I was lucky to rent a room from a student from the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: When seaching for accommodations - start early. It is best to live above the river whereas it is a bit schetchy below the river. Kralingen is a really nice neighbourhood to live in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would be nice if the university had more dorm rooms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to registrate for the courses I wanted to attend. It did not take more than 5 min.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The course catalouge was available and Osiris, which had descibtions of the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted. And we had one week to change course if we did not want them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the process. It was pretty easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the courses was pretty hard. The Erasmus University is known for being hardcore. 
Applied game theory was a lot every week. I spend 10 hourse+ on this course each week. 
Economic history was only once a week, so it was not as hard and there was only one assignment during the block.  
The other courses were duable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same. It had lectures and tutorials for most of the classes. Economic History was the only course without tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economics of Well-being (15 ECTS), Applied game theory (4 ECTS), International Economics (8 ECTS), Economic History (4 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course International economics. It was a mix between finance and trade and it was really interesting. I would also recommend Economics of Well-being which was a minor. It was very different from other economic courses and it was based upon subjective well-being instead of objective well-being.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The local transportation was pretty expensive, so it is nice to rent or bring a bike with you. The food was pretty cheap for a dane.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined a football club and that was really nice in order to talk to dutch students etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports clubs, international clubs for different cuntries, movie clubs etc. There was a lot available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join ESN nights, events etc. Those are nice. And join a club/sport. Then it is easier to become friends woth people and get to know them besides studying.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I traveled a lot in the Netherlands. Go to Utrecht, Antwerpen, Leiden, Gouda, Delft, Amsterdam. Does are really nice cities and they are close by.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was actually pretty easy. The dutch people are very simular to danes so it was kind of the same culture with bikes, buns with cheese etc. And the language is also kind of easy to understand and learn.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is nice to try to learn dutch. That will help you a lot with socializing. Otherwise just be open and try to talk to as many as possible.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the language at the begining.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The bike. They bike everywhere and that was really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Rent a bike
2) Learn dutch
3) join a club/sport

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The school is pretty though so you need to study as well as having fun during your exchange otherwise you won't be able to pass the exams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The football team I joined was really nice. The girls became some of my best friends during my exchange and that was the best part of the exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely to balance school and having fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just remember to enjoy it while you are there. It will be over so fast.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
